conventions.axes: Y-up, right-handed; camera looks down -Z by default; ground is the XZ plane at y = 0
conventions.lightIntensity: three.js physical units (directional/hemisphere/ambient: lux-like; spot/point: candela, decay 2)
conventions.easing: named functions from kit/time.js `ease` (formulas in references/kit-api.md)
conventions.camera: fov is vertical field of view in degrees (three.js convention); sensor-agnostic

style.name: Infinity Mirror
style.description: Recursion you can count: a framed light box on a dark gallery wall holds one real layer (a hoop of large warm and coloured bulbs plus a small glowing figure) between a rear mirror and a half-silvered front glass. Each reflection is REAL instanced geometry (generation n = the real layer reflected n times: alternately flipped, stepped back by the cavity depth, dimmed by mirror x glass reflectance per bounce, so deep copies go dim and green), so the tunnel can grow one generation at a time, anything placed in the real layer ripples into every copy, and the camera can push through the front glass and fly down the tunnel past copy after copy. A small tilt between the mirrors turns every step into a rotation about the mirrors' hinge line: the straight tunnel bends, and at pi/ringCells it closes into a ring, so the flight curves all the way round and arrives back in front of the box. One soft pluck per new generation, each quieter, lower and duller, comes from the same plan.
motion: The tunnel grows one reflection at a time (1, 2, 3 ... then a rush): each new generation fades in a little hot with one pluck, quieter and duller than the last.
Anything placed in the real layer ripples down every generation a few hundredths of a second apart.
The camera pushes through the front glass and flies the tunnel's centreline; exposure follows the generation it is at, so near copies stay readable while their colour drains to green.
Tilting the mirrors bends the tunnel about their hinge line; at pi/ringCells it is a closed ring and the flight ends back in front of the box.

beats.label: A copy of a copy of a copy
A tiny bias bends them all

notes.mechanism: recursion.js: generation n = the real layer reflected n times, T_n = Rot(-n*tilt) Flip^n about the mirrors' hinge line; atten(n) = mirror^ceil(n/2) x glass^floor(n/2); one instance per generation; camera flies the centreline, the ring closes at tilt = pi/ringCells.
